summary: IdP hint canonicalization truncates group claims, dropping RBAC during SSO->proxy handoff
summary_template: SSO login succeeds but RBAC groups absent in downstream token after IdP->proxy handoff
description: Issue summary: After recent IdP metadata refresh, some internal users are able to complete Okta SSO but land in internal portals with no group-based roles. Impact: editors/devs/support reports '403' or reduced privileges in internal-runbook-portal and analytics-portal; blocks runbook access for oncall. Environment: prod-us-west, identity-proxy v2.8.3, auth-service v1.13. Steps to reproduce: 1) Initiate SSO from internal-runbook-portal login button. 2) Choose Okta enterprise IdP (primary). 3) Complete IdP auth; on redirect back to identity-proxy user lands in portal but roles missing. Observed behavior: SAML assertion arrives to identity-proxy with expected GroupClaims, but the identity-proxy logs show the idp_hint value trimmed and percent-decoded incorrectly; the downstream token issued to apps omits groups claim. Expected behavior: idp_hint preserved exactly, group claims forwarded and RBAC mapping applied. This ticket focuses on diagnosing why canonicalization of the idp_hint/EntityID during the proxy handoff strips trailing characters when it contains encoded '+' and double-encoded path segments.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Use Chrome (non-incognito). 2) Navigate to https://internal-runbook-portal.redwood.com/login and click 'Sign in with Okta'. 3) Authenticate as affected user (example: aj@redwood.com). 4) Observe redirect to identity-proxy and final page shows limited role (Viewer) instead of Editor. 5) Check identity-proxy logs at time of login for 'idp_hint' handling entry.
logs_excerpt:
2024-11-12T09:12:03Z identity-proxy: Received SAMLResponse for user aj@redwood.com; idp_hint='https%3A%2F%2Fidp.example.com%2Fokta+org'
2024-11-12T09:12:03Z identity-proxy: Normalized idp_hint='https://idp.example.com/okta' (trimmed '+org')
2024-11-12T09:12:03Z auth-service: Issued OIDC token sub=aj@redwood.com scope=openid profile groups=[]
2024-11-12T09:12:04Z rbac: No mapped group found for user aj@redwood.com; default role Viewer applied
investigation_notes: Timeline: - 2024-11-12 09:00 UTC: Reports start from support channel #internal-auth. - 09:05: triage by Support (Aisha Patel), escalated to identity team. - 09:40: Reproduced by engineering; logs show idp_hint percent-decoding path component containing '+' becomes space then trimmed by URL normalization middleware. Hypothesis: Our identity-proxy includes a URL canonicalizer that runs a library upgrade two weeks ago (go-urilib v1.4.0->v1.5.0) which now aggressively normalizes path tokens and removes characters it considers 'unsafe', inadvertently dropping +encoded suffixes that Okta uses to disambiguate tenant aliases. Corroborating evidence: affected users share IdP alias values containing a '+' (legacy migration from partner tenants). Non-affected IdPs without '+' succeed. Work done: - Pull logs for 50 recent SSO flows, 12/50 show idp_hint modifications. - Reproduced locally by crafting SAML responses with idp_hint containing '%2B' -> normalization trims. - Created minimal repro script and filed related PR to add a unit test in identity-proxy. Risks: All SSO flows with encoded '+' in EntityID might be impacted, which could affect cross-tenant impersonation and delegated admin flows.
comments: Priya Rao (Support): Noted spike in 403s on runbooks; customer-impacting for internal oncall; escalated at 09:05.
Ethan Chen (Identity): Reproduced locally; identity-proxy normalization appears to be the root suspect. Added instrumentation to log raw SAML payload on staging.
Aisha Patel (SRE): Confirmed the library upgrade on 2024-10-31; rolling back library on staging removed the trimming behavior.
Samir Gupta (Security): Concerned about silent dropping of claims; recommends short mitigation (rewrite rule) rather than full rollback to reduce blast radius.
current_workaround: Temporary routing: For affected tenants we configured identity-proxy to bypass the canonicalization middleware via a header-based toggle (applied to us-west only). This restores group claims for ~80% of repro cases. Documented mapping in runbook 'IdP+ canonicalization bypass'.
next_steps: 1) Prepare a targeted patch to identity-proxy that preserves percent-encoded '+' (%2B) in idp_hint and passes unit tests. 2) Submit PR with tests (linked above). 3) Deploy canary to staging and one us-west instance, monitor login success rate and group propagation. 4) Plan full rollout if canary stable; otherwise rollback to previous library version. 5) Longer-term: add end-to-end tests for IdP EntityID variants.
resolution_notes: (Pending) Partial mitigation applied via bypass toggle on 2024-11-12 13:00 UTC. Full fix PR prepared and awaiting code review: https://github.com/redwood-inference/identity-proxy/pull/1427. Post-merge steps include canary and rollback plan. No postmortem required unless issue scope expands to >1% of SSO traffic.
communication_log: Slack thread: #internal-auth thread 'idp hint trimming' started by Priya Rao at 2024-11-12T09:02Z. Pager duty: identity oncall notified. No external customer blasts required since affected users are internal only.
notes_for_oncall: If additional users report missing roles, collect SAMLResponse (base64) and timestamp, avoid asking users to re-provision Okta groups. Use bypass toggle as temporary mitigation and attach to this ticket the timestamped SAMLPayload for further analysis.
